faqs.question: What does the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal DNA in cerebrospinal fluid.

faqs.question: Why is the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF done?
faqs.answer: This test is primarily done to diagnose fungal infections in the central nervous system. It also helps monitor the effectiveness of antifungal treatment. Other reasons to perform this test include identifying fungal species, guiding treatment decisions, and assessing the risk of developing fungal-related complications.

faqs.question: When is the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • This test is recommended for individuals with symptoms or risk factors suggestive of a fungal infection in the central nervous system (e.g., persistent headaches, altered mental status). • Patients with immunocompromised conditions, such as HIV/AIDS or organ transplant recipients, may require this test to rule out fungal infections. • Additionally, patients with suspected meningitis or encephalitis may also undergo this test.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results, i.e., a result indicating the presence of fungal DNA in CSF, suggest the presence of a fungal infection in the central nervous system.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF?
faqs.answer: During this test, a sample of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) will be collected using a sterile, leak-proof container during a lumbar puncture procedure. The CSF sample will then be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • A lumbar puncture procedure will be performed to collect cerebrospinal fluid. • Follow any fasting instructions given by your doctor. • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, including antibiotics or antifungal drugs. • Provide any relevant medical history or clinical details as requested by your doctor. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF include: • Fungal culture: This test helps grow and identify the specific fungal species causing the infection. • Blood tests: To assess the overall health, immune status, and presence of any systemic fungal infections. • Imaging studies, such as MRI or CT scan: To evaluate the extent and location of the infection within the central nervous system.

faqs.question: What is the Panfungal-DNA Detection by PCR & Sanger Sequencing – CSF also known as?
faqs.answer: PCR and Sanger sequencing for fungal DNA in cerebrospinal fluid

faqs.question: What is a fungal infection in the central nervous system?
faqs.answer: A fungal infection in the central nervous system refers to an infection caused by fungi that invade the brain, spinal cord, or meninges. These infections can be serious and may lead to meningitis, encephalitis, or other neurological complications.
